name: browserhive

//scripts.build: Compile TypeScript via `tsc -b` (composite build — picks up tsconfig.generated.json through the `references` array in tsconfig.json), then `build:behaviors`. Output goes to dist/. The `prebuild` lifecycle hook runs `openapi:prep` first.
//scripts.typecheck:behaviors: Type-check the browser-side behavior runtime (src/behaviors/runtime/) against tsconfig.behaviors.json (DOM lib, noEmit). The runtime is excluded from the other tsconfigs (Node lib) and bundled by esbuild, which does not type-check — this is the only place it is actually checked.
//scripts.build:behaviors: Type-check the behavior runtime (typecheck:behaviors) then bundle src/behaviors/runtime/ (browser scripts using window/document/self) into a single injectable IIFE at dist/src/behaviors/runtime.js via esbuild. Runs AFTER tsc and writes under dist/src so the Docker runtime stage (which only copies dist/src) ships it. The runtime dir is excluded from the tsc build.
//scripts.build:examples: Dev-only build for examples/ (data-client). tsconfig.build.json ships only src + bin, so `npm run build` never emits dist/examples — this compiles src + bin + examples via tsconfig.examples.json so `node dist/examples/data-client.js` resolves its `../src/*.js` imports against dist/src. The `prebuild:examples` hook runs `openapi:prep` first (examples import src/http/generated). Requires a running server (host dev loop or the container stack) to accept requests.
//scripts.test: Vitest test runner in single-run mode (see vitest.config.mts for setup). The `pretest` lifecycle hook runs `openapi:prep` first so generated TS is fresh.
//scripts.test:ui: @vitest/ui in watch mode, scoped to the `unit` project. Scoped deliberately: without `--project` Vitest also collects `e2e`, whose globalSetup waits 45s for a running stack and then fails — so a bare `vitest --ui` is unusable unless the stack is up. Use `test:ui:e2e` for that case.
//scripts.test:ui:e2e: @vitest/ui against the `e2e` project. Requires the stack (`container-compose --profile meadow up -d -b`); the globalSetup fails loudly after 45s otherwise. This is where the suite's `annotate()` output is worth looking at — the UI renders it as a Test Annotations panel and inlines it in the Code tab.
//scripts.test:report: Static HTML report for the `unit` project into html/ (needs @vitest/ui). Local convenience only — CI does not build this. Cannot be opened over file://; serve it, e.g. `npx vite preview --outDir html`.
//scripts.test:report:e2e: Static HTML report for the `e2e` project into html-e2e/ — this is what .github/workflows/e2e.yml uploads as the `e2e-report` artifact. Separate output dir so it never mixes with `test:report`. Same file:// caveat: serve it with `npx vite preview --outDir html-e2e`.
//scripts.lint: Top-level orchestrator that runs both `lint:source` (ESLint) and `lint:openapi` (Redocly). Has no `prelint` hook — see the `pre*/post*` notes below.
//scripts.server: Run the compiled HTTP server entry point (`dist/bin/main.js`). Requires `npm run build` to have produced the dist/ output.
//scripts.lint:source: ESLint over the TypeScript sources. Backed by `prelint:source` (= openapi:prep) so the generated `src/http/generated/*` files are fresh before eslint type-checks them via eslint-import-resolver-typescript.
//scripts.lint:openapi: Redocly lint over `src/http/openapi.yaml`. Independent of code generation — runs against the YAML directly, so no `prelint:openapi` hook is needed.
//scripts.prep: Build-prerequisite chain run by the prebuild/pretest/prelint:source hooks: openapi:prep (generated OpenAPI TS) + generate:version (the src/generated/version.ts build fingerprint). Extracted so those hooks do not duplicate it.
//scripts.openapi:prep: Composite of openapi:generate + openapi:gen-operations + openapi:bundle. Part of `prep`. Redocly lint is intentionally NOT part of this chain — it is a contract-quality gate exposed as `lint:openapi`, not a code-generation prerequisite.
//scripts.openapi:generate: Runs @hey-api/openapi-ts (configured by openapi-ts.config.ts) to generate TypeScript types, an operationId-keyed SDK, and a fetch-based client from src/http/openapi.yaml into src/http/generated/.
//scripts.openapi:gen-operations: Generates src/http/generated/operations.gen.ts — a typed OPERATIONS map (operationId → { method, path }) and OperationId union — from src/http/openapi.yaml. Must run AFTER openapi:generate because hey-api cleans the output directory before writing.
//scripts.openapi:bundle: Pre-dereferences src/http/openapi.yaml to dist/openapi.dereferenced.json so the runtime server can wire up Fastify Ajv schemas without depending on @apidevtools/swagger-parser or the source YAML at runtime.
//scripts.openapi:build-docs: Renders the Redoc HTML used as a static, externally published artifact (GitHub Pages workflow). Not required by the runtime server — `/docs` and `/openapi.yaml` are no longer served by the application.
//scripts.generate:version: Writes src/generated/version.ts (BUILD_INFO = { version, revision, buildTime }) surfaced at /v1/status.build. revision = process.env.GIT_REV (how Docker passes it — the build context has no .git) || `git rev-parse --short HEAD` (host) || 'dev'. Generated (gitignored); run as part of `prep`.
//scripts.docs:preview: Local one-shot preview: builds the same Redoc HTML the CI publishes, then prints the absolute file:// URL. Open it in a browser. Self-contained — no local web server needed. (`redocly preview-docs` was removed in @redocly/cli v2; `redocly preview` requires paid Reunite packages and is not used here.)
//scripts.site:dev: Astro/Starlight dev server for the developer handbook in docs-site/ (prose + mermaid + code injected from src/). Distinct from `docs:*`, which renders the OpenAPI/Redoc API reference.
//scripts.site:build: Static build of docs-site/ to docs-site/dist/. ts-morph injects code-derived facts (`@glossary` terms, `// #region` snippets, type tables) from src/ at build time — a missing region or interface fails the build, so injected code cannot drift.
//scripts.site:preview: Serve the built docs-site/dist/ locally (`astro preview`).
//scripts.docs:spec-coverage: Regenerates docs-site/…/spec-coverage.md (en + ja) from test/docs/spec-coverage-data.ts. Run after changing which WARC / WACZ / CDXJ surface the code emits.
//scripts.docs:spec-coverage:check: The CI form: compares instead of writing, and fails if the committed page is stale. The same test also checks the table's `implemented` claims against the field names builders.ts and cdxj.ts actually write, so a coverage table cannot drift from the code it describes.
//scripts.site:check: Docs sync guard (run in CI): `docs:spec-coverage:check`, `site:build`, then scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs. The build catches missing regions/interfaces; the script catches what the build cannot see — `/terminology/#g-<Term>` links whose `@glossary` tag was removed, and `src/….ts` paths that were renamed. Exits red on drift.
pre*/post* hooks: Scripts named `pre<name>` and `post<name>` are npm lifecycle hooks:
when you run `npm run <name>`, npm automatically runs pre<name> first,
//scripts.prebuild: npm lifecycle hook for `build` — runs `prep`. Fires automatically; see the `pre*/post* hooks` note.
//scripts.pretest: npm lifecycle hook for `test` — runs `prep`. Fires automatically; see the `pre*/post* hooks` note.
//scripts.pretest:ui / pretest:report: npm lifecycle hooks for the two `unit`-scoped UI scripts — both run `prep`, same as `pretest`. The e2e variants deliberately have no hook: like `test:e2e`, they talk to the stack over HTTP only and import no generated TS, so `prep` would be wasted work.
//scripts.prelint:source: npm lifecycle hook for `lint:source` — runs `prep`. Fires automatically; see the `pre*/post* hooks` note.

scripts.stack:up: MEADOW_TAG=$(git -C meadow describe --tags) MEADOW_REV=$(git -C meadow rev-parse --short HEAD) GIT_TAG=$(git describe --tags) GIT_REV=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) container-compose --profile meadow --profile signing up -d -b
scripts.test:e2e: pnpm --filter meadow build && vitest run --project e2e
scripts.test:report:e2e: pnpm --filter meadow build && vitest run --project e2e --reporter=html --outputFile.html=html-e2e/index.html
scripts.lint: pnpm run lint:source && pnpm run lint:openapi
scripts.prep: pnpm run openapi:prep && pnpm run generate:version
scripts.openapi:prep: pnpm run openapi:generate && pnpm run openapi:gen-operations && pnpm run openapi:bundle
scripts.docs:preview: pnpm run openapi:build-docs && node -e "console.log('Open file://' + require('path').resolve('dist/docs/index.html') + ' in your browser')"
scripts.site:check: pnpm run docs:spec-coverage:check && pnpm run site:build && node scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs
scripts.prelint:source: pnpm run prep && pnpm --filter meadow build

//dependencies.fastify: Fast, low-overhead HTTP framework with native JSON Schema validation (Ajv).
//dependencies.ajv: JSON Schema validator. Pinned at the root so transitive resolutions land on v8 (matches Fastify's bundled compiler).
//dependencies.puppeteer: Headless browser library. Used at runtime via puppeteer-extra to connect to remote Chromium servers.
//dependencies.puppeteer-extra: Puppeteer wrapper that allows plugins. Used with stealth plugin to avoid bot detection.
//dependencies.puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth: Stealth plugin for puppeteer-extra. Applies various evasion techniques to avoid headless browser detection.
//dependencies.yaml: YAML 1.2 parser used by examples/data-client.ts to read data/*.yaml fixtures (replaces the previous CSV format so entries can carry inline comments).

//devDependencies.@apidevtools/swagger-parser: Pre-dereferences openapi.yaml at build time (scripts/openapi-bundle.mjs). The output JSON is shipped instead of the YAML, so this is build-time only — not required at runtime.
//devDependencies.@hey-api/openapi-ts: Generates TypeScript types, operationId-keyed SDK functions, and a fetch-based client from openapi.yaml. Output is src/http/generated/. Replaces openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch (one tool for both type and runtime client).
//devDependencies.@redocly/cli: OpenAPI linter / preview / docs generator. Configured via redocly.yaml at the repo root; surfaced via `lint:openapi` (a sibling of `lint:source` under the top-level `lint` orchestrator) and the openapi.yml CI workflow.
//devDependencies.esbuild: Bundles the browser-side behavior runtime (src/behaviors/runtime/) into one injectable IIFE (see the build:behaviors script). Build-time only — the prebuilt bundle ships in dist/src, so esbuild is not needed in the Docker runtime stage.
//devDependencies.@types/estree: Required for TypeScript type resolution. Transitive dependency from eslint and rollup (via vite).
//devDependencies.@types/json-schema: Required for TypeScript type resolution. Transitive dependency from @eslint/core.
//devDependencies.@types/node: Required for TypeScript type resolution. Transitive dependency from vitest and vite.
//devDependencies.@types/yauzl: Required for TypeScript type resolution. Transitive dependency from puppeteer via extract-zip.

puppeteer-extra-plugin-user-data-dir > r: puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth depends on user-preferences -> user-data-dir -> rimraf@3.
rimraf@3 pulls in deprecated glob@7 and inflight@1, causing npm ci warnings.
The puppeteer-extra monorepo is unmaintained since March 2023 (GitHub Issue #914).
We override rimraf to the project-level v6 ($rimraf) to eliminate these warnings.
rimraf v4+ has a breaking API change (Promise instead of callback), but this is safe
because we disable the stealth user-agent-override evasion in src/browser.ts,
so user-data-dir's rimraf call (deleteUserDataDir) is never executed at runtime.
js-yaml: which is in the vulnerable range (high: quadratic-complexity DoS via merge
keys / repeated aliases). npm audit fix cannot touch it (it would need to
bump hey-api). Force js-yaml to ^4.3.0 (the fixed 4.x) everywhere.
Kept on 4.x — 5.x is a major hey-api/swagger-parser do not expect; 4.3.0
is API-compatible and clears the advisory (verified: build + tests pass).
Remove this once @hey-api ships json-schema-ref-parser with a fixed js-yaml.
brace-expansion: Reached through several tool chains (minimatch, glob). <=5.0.7 has an
unbounded-expansion DoS; 5.0.8 fixes it and is API-compatible.
Remove once the parents depend on the fixed range themselves.
